title: Optimized Surgical Workflow and Real-Time Quality Assessment via Intraoperative Digital Volume Tomography
summary:
This study investigates whether a special type of X-ray imaging performed during surgery – called intraoperative cone-beam computed tomography (iCBCT) – can improve the treatment of patients undergoing neurosurgical procedures.
Currently, control imaging is usually done one day after surgery. With the new method, it is possible to check during the ongoing operation whether, for example, a brain hemorrhage has been fully removed or a drainage catheter has been placed correctly. This allows potential issues to be identified and corrected immediately, without the need for a second anesthesia or another operation.
The technique may also be beneficial for patients undergoing stereotactic brain biopsies, where a complex preoperative CT scan would no longer be necessary. 
In the study, patients who receive iCBCT will be compared to a retrospective group previously treated with the standard approach involving postoperative imaging.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- intracerebral hemorrhage with indication for surgical evacuation
- Shunt implantation procedures
- stereotactic biopsies or biopsies performed using Varioguide
Exclusion criteria:
- Minors (under 18 years of age)
